map.reason: Change appears in distinct patches, so outlines carry the meaning.

known_confusions: Radar shadow behind terrain and tall buildings is dark and can read as water.
Smooth dry surfaces such as tarmac, sand flats and bare hardpan can read as water.
Flooded vegetation may NOT be detected: the canopy scatters the radar pulse back to the sensor, so water beneath trees or tall crops is frequently missed.
Wind roughens open water and raises backscatter, which can cause flooding to be underestimated during a storm.
Boundary vintage is 2015; districts created after that date are not resolvable.

report.text: The Sentinel‑1 analysis shows a total flooded extent of 486.4 km² [E1], which is 1.4 percent of the observable area [E2]. Compared with the baseline period, net new water is 477.9 km² [E8] and the permanent water area is 273.5 km² [E3]. The 25 largest zones cover 44.2 percent of the flood extent, with the biggest zone measuring 25.73 km² [E5] and a total of 98 zones identified [E4]. This detection method scores IoU 0.441, precision 0.763 and recall 0.511 on Sen1Floods11 HandLabeled (446 chips, VV); roughly a quarter of detected pixels are expected to be false positives, and around half of true flooding is expected to be missed.
